en.title: EDF Save Editor
en.save_paths_info: Copy these EDF save directories (may adjust per install):
en.save_paths_howto_1: 1. "Load Save" opens straight to your most likely save folder - it auto-detects vanilla vs. modded folder names, checks OneDrive-redirected installs, and jumps into whichever SAVESLOT0X profile you touched most recently.
en.save_paths_howto_2: 2. Browse into a different EDF game's folder than what's selected above and the Game dropdown switches to match automatically (EDF5/EDF4.1 will ask Online or Offline first, since that can't be told from the folder name alone).
en.save_paths_howto_3: 3. The rows above are reference paths for browsing manually or backing up your saves - "Copy" puts a path on your clipboard to paste into File Explorer's address bar.
en.save_paths_howto_4: 4. After loading, edit values in the sections below (Armor, Loadouts, Color Customization, Weapon Table, Mission Table, Achievements) and click "Save" at the top to write changes back to the loaded file.
en.save_paths_howto_5: 5. Always keep a backup of your save before experimenting - edits here are byte-level and unforgiving of mistakes.
en.save_paths_howto_6: 6. Don't be shy about the Translation Editor - it's the button next to Save Paths, collapsed by default; expand it to add a new language, or fix up any text in this tool that looks wrong for UI Strings, Weapon Names, or Mission Names.
en.save_paths_howto_7: 7. Wanted: PlayStation save samples. This tool currently only supports PC/Steam saves - if you can pull a PS4/PS5 EDF save file (e.g. via Save Wizard or a similar export tool), sharing a copy would let us add PlayStation support.

en.purpose: Per-mode, per-difficulty curve endpoints for the REAL (gameplay-side) weapon drop level band -- consumed by EDFWeaponFarming.py's compute_level_band(). This is a DIFFERENT curve than the community wiki's 'Weapon Level Limit' (Online Room Setting display, x25-scaled) -- see the RE writeup below.
en.formula_status: VERIFIED live via Ghidra MCP, RE session 2026-08-14 (WeaponDropLevelBand_Compute @ 0x1800d7c40, WeaponDropLevelBand_ReadDifficultyCurve @ 0x1800e26c0): level_max = min_endpoint + (max_endpoint - min_endpoint) * progress; level_min = max(0, level_max - band_width); progress = mission_index / (mission_count - 1).
en.numeric_values_status: POPULATED 2026-08-14 from the community wiki (KCreator/Earth-Defence-Force-Documentation, EDF6-Advanced-menu-Setup, 'Weapon Drop Rate' section) -- the wiki's SGO field there is literally named {{{WeaponDrops}}}, matching the sub-field name predicted in WeaponDropLevelBand_ReadDifficultyCurve's doc BEFORE this data was found. Source: https://github.com/KCreator/Earth-Defence-Force-Documentation/wiki/EDF6-Advanced-menu-Setup-(ENG)#weapon-drop-rate . Cross-checked against WeaponDropData_EDF6.json (real per-weapon P4): for every filled-in cell below, every one of 147/19/40 missions has at least 1 eligible weapon and the band stays inside P4's real observed range (0.0-3.8 base, ~4.0-4.7 DLC1/2) -- see 'scale_note' below for why these are used RAW, not x25'd.
en.scale_note: The wiki's page header says 'The values will be multiplied by 25' -- but WeaponDropLevelBand_Compute's decompile has NO x25 (or any) scale multiply anywhere, and the raw wiki numbers already land in the exact same range as WEAPONTABLE.json's real P4 field. Multiplying by 25 first would put every value far outside P4's range (0-4.7) and make EVERY mission show zero eligible weapons, which contradicts a working drop table. Conclusion: values below are used RAW/unscaled for this specific curve; the wiki's x25 note most likely describes the sibling online-room-setting 'Weapon Level Limit' curve (WeaponLevelLimitInterpolator @ 0x1800e2710, separately confirmed x25 in Session 44) rather than this one. Flagging for anyone re-checking: if in-game testing ever shows this assumption wrong, multiply every min_endpoint/max_endpoint/band_width below by 25 and re-test.
en.known_data_gap: EDF6 DLC2 / Normal (difficulty 2) is intentionally left null -- the wiki page's raw source has THREE mutually-conflicting candidate triples for that one cell ([0.5,1,0.2] and [1,1.5,0.2] and [1.775,2.5,0.25], from three different overlapping row labels in the same table). Rather than guess, this cell stays unset until confirmed (in-game testing, or a cleaner extraction of config.sgo). All other 14 of 15 mode/difficulty cells are unambiguous in the wiki source.
en.struct_path: difficulty node via +0x18->+0x54->node+len->difficulty*0xc (same as WeaponLevelLimitInterpolator); this curve's own sub-array at node+0x20, floats at +0x20/+0x2c/+0x38 = [min_endpoint, max_endpoint, band_width].

en.modded_gain_note: Preview only - simulates your armor gain rate at this multiplier. Does not get written to your save; only 'Total You Really Have' below is.
en.armor_note:
'Total You Really Have' is your accumulated armor-pickup score for this class (the game's own running total from armor drops) - not your HP. It's the exact value written to your save (both MAX and current armor), so type your final target score, not an armor-up count.
Base Game Gain / Modded Armor Gain (blue / orange) are read-only previews of the HP bonus that score converts to via normal in-game armor-up progression; neither one gets saved.
+100/-100 edit 'Total You Really Have' directly (won't go below 0). Changes apply immediately - no need to revisit Class / Equipment in-game to activate them.
Color key: purple = a value you type in that gets saved. The same purple marks the Loadout weapon-ID fields and the Weapon Farming curve fields elsewhere in this tool.
en.color_panel_warning: Colors are stored as raw RGBA float32 (normally 0.0-1.0). 'Pick' sets RGB via a color picker (capped at 1.0); Alpha is edited separately and is 1.0 (fully opaque) on essentially every palette we've seen. For the 'NEON' glow effect (in-game color UI's Saturation/Value slider pushed above 100), type R/G/B values above 1.0 directly into the fields instead of using Pick.
en.mission_table_note: Tip: Double-click a cell to toggle Completed/Not Completed. Unlock/Reset (right) applies a whole difficulty at once, for the active class only.

Rows marked (unverified) are predicted slot positions, not individually confirmed - see EDF5_SAVE_FORMAT_NOTES.md before relying on one of those for anything that matters.

ja.title: EDFセーブエディタ
ja.save_paths_info: 以下のEDFセーブフォルダをコピーできます（インストール環境により異なる場合があります）：
ja.save_paths_howto_1: 1.「セーブを読み込む」を押すと、最も可能性の高いセーブフォルダが自動で開きます－無印／MOD版のフォルダ名を自動判別し、OneDriveへリダイレクトされたインストールも確認したうえで、最後に触れたSAVESLOT0Xプロファイルへ直接ジャンプします。
ja.save_paths_howto_2: 2. 上で選択中とは別のEDF作品のフォルダを開くと、ゲームのドロップダウンが自動的に切り替わります（EDF5／EDF4.1はフォルダ名だけではオンライン／オフラインを判別できないため、先に確認が入ります）。
ja.save_paths_howto_3: 3. 上の各行は、手動でフォルダを開いたりセーブをバックアップしたりする際の参考パスです－「Copy」を押すとパスがクリップボードにコピーされ、エクスプローラーのアドレスバーに貼り付けられます。
ja.save_paths_howto_4: 4. 読み込み後は下の各セクション（アーマー、現在の装備、カラーカスタマイズ、武器一覧、ミッションテーブル、実績／トロフィー）で値を編集し、上部の「上書き保存」を押すと変更が読み込んだファイルに書き戻されます。
ja.save_paths_howto_5: 5. 試す前には必ずセーブのバックアップを取ってください－この編集はバイト単位で行われ、間違えても元に戻せません。
ja.save_paths_howto_6: 6. 翻訳エディタも遠慮なく使ってください－「セーブパス」の隣にあるボタンで、初期状態では折りたたまれています。展開すると新しい言語を追加したり、UI文字列・武器名・ミッション名でおかしいと感じたテキストを修正したりできます。
ja.save_paths_howto_7: 7. Wanted: PlayStation save samples. This tool currently only supports PC/Steam saves - if you can pull a PS4/PS5 EDF save file (e.g. via Save Wizard or a similar export tool), sharing a copy would let us add PlayStation support.

kr.title: EDF 세이브 에디터
kr.save_paths_info: 다음 EDF 세이브 폴더를 복사할 수 있습니다 (설치 환경에 따라 다를 수 있습니다):
kr.save_paths_howto_1: 1. '세이브 불러오기'를 누르면 가장 가능성이 높은 세이브 폴더가 바로 열립니다－바닐라와 모드 폴더 이름을 자동으로 구분하고, OneDrive로 리디렉션된 설치도 확인한 뒤, 가장 최근에 사용한 SAVESLOT0X 프로필로 바로 이동합니다.
kr.save_paths_howto_2: 2. 위에서 선택된 것과 다른 EDF 게임 폴더를 열면 게임 드롭다운이 자동으로 전환됩니다 (EDF5/EDF4.1은 폴더 이름만으로 온라인/오프라인을 구분할 수 없어 먼저 확인을 요청합니다).
kr.save_paths_howto_3: 3. 위의 각 행은 수동으로 폴더를 열거나 세이브를 백업할 때 참고할 경로입니다－'Copy'를 누르면 경로가 클립보드에 복사되어 파일 탐색기 주소창에 붙여넣을 수 있습니다.
kr.save_paths_howto_4: 4. 불러온 후에는 아래 각 섹션(아머, 장비, 색상 커스터마이징, 무기 목록, 미션 테이블, 업적)에서 값을 편집하고, 상단의 '저장'을 눌러 변경 사항을 불러온 파일에 다시 기록하세요.
kr.save_paths_howto_5: 5. 시도하기 전에는 항상 세이브를 백업해 두세요－이 편집은 바이트 단위로 이루어지며 실수에 관대하지 않습니다.
kr.save_paths_howto_6: 6. 번역 편집기도 편하게 사용해 보세요－'저장 경로' 옆에 있는 버튼으로, 기본적으로 접혀 있습니다. 펼치면 새 언어를 추가하거나, UI 문자열・무기 이름・미션 이름 중 이상해 보이는 텍스트를 직접 수정할 수 있습니다.
kr.save_paths_howto_7: 7. Wanted: PlayStation save samples. This tool currently only supports PC/Steam saves - if you can pull a PS4/PS5 EDF save file (e.g. via Save Wizard or a similar export tool), sharing a copy would let us add PlayStation support.
kr.loadout_note: 팁: 이 입력란에 무기 ID 번호를 입력하세요. ID는 '무기 목록' 탭에 표시되는 'ID' 열과 동일합니다.

kr.purpose: Per-mode, per-difficulty curve endpoints for the REAL (gameplay-side) weapon drop level band -- consumed by EDFWeaponFarming.py's compute_level_band(). This is a DIFFERENT curve than the community wiki's 'Weapon Level Limit' (Online Room Setting display, x25-scaled) -- see the RE writeup below.
kr.formula_status: VERIFIED live via Ghidra MCP, RE session 2026-08-14 (WeaponDropLevelBand_Compute @ 0x1800d7c40, WeaponDropLevelBand_ReadDifficultyCurve @ 0x1800e26c0): level_max = min_endpoint + (max_endpoint - min_endpoint) * progress; level_min = max(0, level_max - band_width); progress = mission_index / (mission_count - 1).
kr.numeric_values_status: POPULATED 2026-08-14 from the community wiki (KCreator/Earth-Defence-Force-Documentation, EDF6-Advanced-menu-Setup, 'Weapon Drop Rate' section) -- the wiki's SGO field there is literally named {{{WeaponDrops}}}, matching the sub-field name predicted in WeaponDropLevelBand_ReadDifficultyCurve's doc BEFORE this data was found. Source: https://github.com/KCreator/Earth-Defence-Force-Documentation/wiki/EDF6-Advanced-menu-Setup-(ENG)#weapon-drop-rate . Cross-checked against WeaponDropData_EDF6.json (real per-weapon P4): for every filled-in cell below, every one of 147/19/40 missions has at least 1 eligible weapon and the band stays inside P4's real observed range (0.0-3.8 base, ~4.0-4.7 DLC1/2) -- see 'scale_note' below for why these are used RAW, not x25'd.
kr.scale_note: The wiki's page header says 'The values will be multiplied by 25' -- but WeaponDropLevelBand_Compute's decompile has NO x25 (or any) scale multiply anywhere, and the raw wiki numbers already land in the exact same range as WEAPONTABLE.json's real P4 field. Multiplying by 25 first would put every value far outside P4's range (0-4.7) and make EVERY mission show zero eligible weapons, which contradicts a working drop table. Conclusion: values below are used RAW/unscaled for this specific curve; the wiki's x25 note most likely describes the sibling online-room-setting 'Weapon Level Limit' curve (WeaponLevelLimitInterpolator @ 0x1800e2710, separately confirmed x25 in Session 44) rather than this one. Flagging for anyone re-checking: if in-game testing ever shows this assumption wrong, multiply every min_endpoint/max_endpoint/band_width below by 25 and re-test.
kr.known_data_gap: EDF6 DLC2 / Normal (difficulty 2) is intentionally left null -- the wiki page's raw source has THREE mutually-conflicting candidate triples for that one cell ([0.5,1,0.2] and [1,1.5,0.2] and [1.775,2.5,0.25], from three different overlapping row labels in the same table). Rather than guess, this cell stays unset until confirmed (in-game testing, or a cleaner extraction of config.sgo). All other 14 of 15 mode/difficulty cells are unambiguous in the wiki source.
kr.struct_path: difficulty node via +0x18->+0x54->node+len->difficulty*0xc (same as WeaponLevelLimitInterpolator); this curve's own sub-array at node+0x20, floats at +0x20/+0x2c/+0x38 = [min_endpoint, max_endpoint, band_width].

cn.numeric_values_status: POPULATED 2026-08-14 from the community wiki (KCreator/Earth-Defence-Force-Documentation, EDF6-Advanced-menu-Setup, 'Weapon Drop Rate' section) -- the wiki's SGO field there is literally named {{{WeaponDrops}}}, matching the sub-field name predicted in WeaponDropLevelBand_ReadDifficultyCurve's doc BEFORE this data was found.
